content: Table TABREF17 shows phone classification and speaker recognition results for the three model configurations: the VAE baseline, the CJFS encoder and the CJFA encoder. In our experiments the window size was set to 30 frames, namely 10 frames for the target and 10 frames for left and right neighbours, and an embedding dimension of 150. This was used for both CJFS and CJFA models alike. Results show that the CJFA encoder obtains significantly better phone classification accuracy than the VAE baseline and also than the CJFS encoder. These results are replicated for speaker recognition tasks. The CJFA encoder performs better on all tasks than the VAE baseline by a significant margin. It is noteworthy that performance on Task b is generally significantly lower than for Task a, for reasons of training overlap but also smaller training set sizes.
